statements.action_statement: No fixed release is available yet; update when Docker Hardened Images publishes one.
statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-35190 ("Out-of-Bounds Read in TLS 1.3 Key-Share Processing with Suite B Certificate Flag", Low): a TLS 1.3 server whose application sets the Suite B certificate flag with SSL_CTX_set_cert_flags() can read past the end of a fixed group list when a ClientHello offers no Suite B group; default configurations do not reach this code, and the code is in libssl, outside the FIPS module boundary. It affects OpenSSL 3.5 and is fixed upstream for OpenSSL 3.5.10 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20261117.txt) by https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/9491b0d9cc7950af1f3dc89499bd5433b9cd4f43 on the 3.5 branch, which makes tls1_get_group_tuples() return a Suite B tuple matching the fixed group list (new static tables suiteb_tuples_both and suiteb_tuples_one in ssl/t1_lib.c) and adds a bounds check to tls_parse_ctos_key_share(). Debian lists trixie as vulnerable, including 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-35190). DHI backported that commit into its Debian 13 openssl builds from the fourth published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 on, and the rebuild of Debian 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 carries it too; the FIPS builds do not. Evidence, from the libssl.so.3 debug symbols in libssl3t64-dbgsym of every published build (24 versions, amd64 and arm64, from the DHI Debian repository and the DHI security repository): suiteb_tuples_both and suiteb_tuples_one are defined in the fourth rebuild of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and in the rebuild of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1, and in no other build, including every FIPS build (3.5.6-1~deb13u1 to 3.5.9-1~deb13u1); suiteb_curves and tls_parse_ctos_key_share are found in every one of those files as a control. Each FIPS build sorts above the non-FIPS rebuilds of the same Debian version, so the range reopens at the FIPS build of 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, closes at the rebuild of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 and reopens at the FIPS build of 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. The status is AFFECTED because the newest FIPS build is still unfixed. The openssl-provider-fips packages hold the FIPS provider module (fips.so) and its documentation, not libssl: their fips.so is the OpenSSL 3.5.5 to 3.5.9 provider in the non-FIPS builds and the OpenSSL 3.1.2 provider in the FIPS builds, and the advisory places the vulnerable code outside the FIPS module boundary.
